overview.description: Integrate Thinkst Canary tokens into the portfolio website to detect unauthorized access, security scanning, and potential attacks. Get real-time email notifications when canary tokens are triggered.
overview.problem: Portfolio websites are public targets for scanners, bots, and malicious actors. Without detection mechanisms, we have no visibility into who is probing our infrastructure.
overview.solution: Deploy canary tokens as tripwires throughout the site — decoy endpoints, fake files, and hidden triggers that alert us via email when accessed.
overview.value: Early detection of security threats, understanding of attack patterns, and a professional security posture that showcases enterprise-grade thinking.

whatAreCanaryTokens.description: Canary tokens are digital tripwires. When someone accesses a canary token (a URL, file, DNS entry, etc.), it sends you an alert. Think of them as alarm sensors for your digital infrastructure.
howItWorks: 1. Create a canary token on canarytokens.org
2. Deploy it in your infrastructure (URL, file, DNS, etc.)
3. When someone accesses it, Thinkst sends you an email
4. You know someone is where they shouldn't be

reasons: Detect port scanners and vulnerability scanners hitting the site
Identify bots crawling for sensitive files (wp-admin, .env, etc.)
Monitor for unauthorized API access attempts
Create decoy admin panels that alert when accessed
Showcase security awareness to future employers

considerations: Canary tokens should never be linked to real sensitive data
Token triggers should be logged but not expose real secrets
Rate limit canary endpoints to prevent abuse
Monitor for false positives (search engine crawlers, etc.)
bestPractices: Use realistic but fake data in canary files
Make canary endpoints look like real admin panels
Add canary tokens to robots.txt to prevent crawler access
Log all trigger attempts for security analysis
Set up alerts for multiple rapid triggers (attack detection)

manualTests: Access canary endpoint and verify email received
